4) PROSE — lede/frame claims all supported. 'historia de la escritura' not 'sucesión … de escuelas, autores y obras maestras' (L85-88); 'literatura emergente' (L77); 'cultura impresa' at the Tragicomedia (L74-75). Cross-source attribution CHECKED AND ACCURATE: the frame says the eyebrow's 'Literaturas Hispánicas' comes from the parent Letras node, not this program — /Users/tomb/p/learn/nodes/uba.ffyl.letras.json:191 does read "eyebrow": "Área · Literaturas Hispánicas" over the exit at :195. The frame's disclaimer that the program states neither the number of cátedras nor the ciclo is correct. All six declared ERRATAS verified literally: 2.4 unpunctuated (L121), 7.3 missing period (L165), items 38/43 surname-only 'Russell'/'Duby' (L459, L519), 'Bagatto Lihri' (L575), U7 Fuentes opening with the unnamed Whinnom Obras completas I before the 'Cárcel de Amor' subheading (L714-716), Pavis printed 'Paidós' (L681-682) and 'Piados' (L774-775). All seven TP topics cited in the frame are literal (TP2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11).

5) EXCLUSIONS — the strong claim 'los 62 ítems … son sin excepción artículos … ninguno es un volumen exento' survives an item-by-item check: every one of the 62 carries a quoted article/chapter title. I specifically probed the likeliest counterexamples — #34 Joset 'Interpretar, interpretar' (a chapter in his own Nuevas investigaciones, L362-363), #38 Russell (chapter in his own Temas de La Celestina, L459-461), #43 Duby (chapter in Historia de las mujeres III, L519-520), #7 and #55 (fichas de cátedra) — all are chapters/fichas, not standalone monographs. No counterexample found. The complementary/general shelves the frame declares out-of-scope do contain the named monographs (Zumthor L221, Blecua L212/L737, Curtius L742, Huizinga L759, Gómez Redondo L753-755), so that sentence is accurate as a joint claim about both shelves.

6) COUNTS — metadata.unidades 7 = 7 spine exits; metadata.bibliografia 26 = 26 book exits; metadata.trabajosPracticos 11 = 11 printed TPs; meta[] tiles ('7', '+ 11 TP', '96 hs') agree with metadata. No count drift.

ADVISORY (none rise to a refutation, all non-fabricating):
(a) The lede enumerates the Primera Sección texts but omits Milagros de Nuestra Señora, which is both a Fuentes text of Unidad 3 (three editions drawn) and named in the fundamentación (L59). An omission, not a false claim, but the one conspicuous gap.
(b) Silent normalizations of original spellings, in a node that otherwise declares it records rarezas: the program prints 'cuadernavía' as one word at 3.2 (L126) while lede and map read 'cuaderna vía'; U4 Fuentes prints 'Serès, Guillermo' (L447) while the exit reads 'G. Serés' (the extract does use 'Serés' elsewhere, L402/L720).
(c) metadata.bibliografia = 26 is a Fuentes-editions count, not a bibliography count (the program's bibliography is 62 obligatoria plus ~150 complementaria/general). The books-group note explains it, but the field name alone would mislead a reader of metadata only.
(d) Map line for Unidad 6, 'misoginia y profeminismo · Grisel y Mirabella': 'misoginia y profeminismo' is literal at 6.2 (L156), but Grisel y Mirabella does not appear in contenidos 6.1-6.3 — it is grounded in U6's Fuentes (L574-575) and TP9 (L180). Grounded, but from a different part of the program than the neighbouring token.
(e) Mild tension between the two rationales: obligatoria items are excluded partly on 'ninguno es un volumen exento', yet three drawn books are page-ranges inside volumes (Santillana pp.135-155 and pp.202-227; San Pedro Obras completas I pp.173-183). Consistent with the actually-declared rule ('las ediciones listadas bajo Fuentes'), so not an inconsistency — the node also discloses each page range.

Not refuted, just not confirmable without the network.
